Order 
This is an application for regular bail under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the 2nd accused in Crime No.1248 of 2023 of Kayamkulam Police Station, Alappuzha District,
registered under Sections 406 and 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The prosecution allegation is that the petitioner along with accused Nos.1 and 3, in furtherance of their common intention to cheat the defacto complainant and to grab money from him, promising Beena vs State Of Kerala on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146921677/
1 admission to students in nursing colleges, received Rs.93 lakhs from him to their accounts.

sentences.text: After receiving the amounts, they neither arranged any admission nor returned the money.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Public Prosecutor were heard.

4. Learned Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the Bail Application stating that the petitioner herein played a major role in cheating the defacto complainant and the students, who aspired for getting admission in nursing colleges.
Initially Rs.93 lakhs was transferred into the account of the 1st accused but later Rs.63 lakhs was transferred into the account of the petitioner herein.

Learned Public Prosecutor submitted that with the money received from the defacto complainant, the petitioner was staying in luxurious hotels and she purchased gold as well as costly vehicles and she transferred amounts to the accounts of her daughter and husband.

Since the amount involved is huge, and two more crimes are pending against the petitioner registered for similar offences, one at Mavelikkara Police Station and another at Puthencruz Police Station, if she is released on bail, she may repeat similar offences.
Therefore, this Court is not inclined to release the petitioner at present.

Sd/-
